# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration (dual-write/dual-run architecture), allowing users to be cut over in controlled batches with a fallback path at every stage. Total population: 40,000 users.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — 800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed a full integration test suite (invoicing, payment capture, refunds, tax calculation, dunning) in staging with 100% parity against legacy outputs on a replayed sample of at least 5,000 historical transactions; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end at least once.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (e.g., monthly-invoice, non-critical accounts). Manual monitoring, daily reconciliation between old and new systems.

**Duration:** 1–2 weeks minimum, or until success criteria below are met.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (25% of users — 10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed with zero unresolved critical (P1) incidents for 7 consecutive days, payment failure rate for migrated users within 0.1 percentage points of legacy baseline, and support ticket volume from migrated users not exceeding 1.5x the pre-migration baseline rate.

**Scope:** Broader mix of customer segments (varied plan types, geographies, payment methods) migrated in sub-batches of ~2,000 users every 2–3 days, with reconciliation checks between each sub-batch.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (73% of users — remaining ~29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed with cumulative billing discrepancy rate under 0.05% of transactions, zero data-integrity incidents requiring manual correction for the trailing 14 days, and finance sign-off confirming reconciled ledgers match between old and new systems for all Phase 2 cohorts.

**Scope:** All remaining users, migrated in weekly waves (e.g., 5,000–8,000 users/week) segmented by risk profile (highest-value/most complex accounts migrated last within this phase).

**Duration:** 4–6 weeks.

**Note:** The old billing system remains fully operational, receiving no removal, disabling, or decommissioning action during Phase 3 or in the batch that completes the final user migration. Decommissioning of the legacy system is a separate, subsequent phase (Phase 4: Legacy Decommission), gated on a minimum 30-day parallel-run stabilization period post-completion of Phase 3, a full final audit, and explicit sign-off from Finance, Engineering, and Support leadership.

---

## Risks

RISK: Payment processing failures spike for migrated users due to misconfigured payment gateway credentials in the new system | Run automated pre-migration validation of gateway credentials and a $0/small-value test-charge for each account before full cutover | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems causes customers to be billed incorrectly (double-billed or under-billed) | Implement automated daily reconciliation jobs comparing invoices/charges across both systems with alerting on any mismatch | Billing Platform Team Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by a surge in billing-related tickets during a batch cutover | Pre-brief support team on migration schedule, provide runbooks and a rollback script, and staff extra on-call coverage during each batch window | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback from new system back to old system fails or causes data loss for an in-flight batch | Require a tested, scripted rollback procedure validated in staging before each phase begins, and freeze new-system writes during rollback execution | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Regulatory/tax calculation errors in new system lead to compliance exposure in certain jurisdictions | Run parallel tax calculations for all migrated accounts for the first 30 days and have Finance/Legal review discrepancies weekly | Finance & Compliance Lead

---

## Halt Criteria (Metric Thresholds)

The rollout must be paused immediately, and the current batch held (with rollback considered), if any of the following occur:

- **Payment failure rate** for migrated users exceeds **1.0%** of attempted transactions in any 24-hour window (vs. legacy baseline).
- **Billing discrepancy rate** (mismatches found in reconciliation) exceeds **0.5%** of migrated transactions in any single batch.
- **P1/critical incident count** related to the new billing system exceeds **2 in a rolling 24-hour period**.

Any halt triggers an incident review before the next batch or phase may proceed.

PHASES: 3
